tools.list_devices: Read-only lookup of devices owned by the authenticated account. No external state change and no open-ended public entity access.
tools.get_device: Read-only lookup of one authenticated account device. No state change and no open-world access.
tools.list_files: Read-only listing inside an authorized private device root. It is bounded to the user's device rather than the public internet.
tools.get_file_metadata: Read-only metadata lookup inside an authorized private device root.
tools.read_file: Read-only content retrieval from an authorized private device path.
tools.write_file: Writes or overwrites an authorized file, so it is not read-only and is potentially destructive. It remains bounded to the private device root.
tools.patch_file: Modifies existing file content and can overwrite prior data, so it is destructive. Hash preconditions reduce but do not remove that property.
tools.search_files: Read-only search within authorized private roots; it does not search the public internet.
tools.run_command: Starts a local command that may change host state and, after explicit bounded approval, code can interact with external entities. Conservative destructive/open-world annotations are intentional.
tools.start_process: Starts a stateful local process that may have irreversible side effects and approved code can interact externally. Conservative destructive/open-world annotations are intentional.
tools.read_process_output: Read-only retrieval of output/state from a managed private process.
tools.write_process_input: Sends input to a running process and can trigger irreversible behavior, including behavior that reaches external entities; conservative destructive/open-world annotations are intentional.
tools.cancel_process: Cancels a managed process. Cancellation can be irreversible, so destructive is true; the action itself is bounded to a private managed process.
tools.list_managed_processes: Read-only listing of Telechir-managed processes on an authorized private device.
tools.get_git_status: Read-only local Git inspection. Network and remote Git writes are outside the capability.
tools.get_git_diff: Read-only local Git diff inspection. It does not modify the repository or access open-ended public entities.
tools.capture_screen: Read-only one-shot capture of the authorized device desktop. It observes private on-device visual state, is bounded, and does not itself change external state.
tools.control_computer: Executes exactly one typed local mouse or keyboard action after CRITICAL local-device confirmation. It can cause irreversible application effects and can indirectly affect external entities through the focused application, so destructive and open-world are conservatively true.
tools.open_browser_session: Creates one isolated ephemeral local BrowserContext without importing the user's browser profile, cookies, storage state, or credentials. It changes local Telechir session state but does not itself navigate to or mutate an external entity.
tools.get_browser_snapshot: Read-only semantic snapshot of the current isolated browser page. The returned page content is untrusted data, but the tool itself does not mutate the page or external state.
tools.navigate_browser: Navigates the isolated browser to a public HTTP(S) destination through Telechir's anti-SSRF egress policy. Navigation reaches open-ended external entities, so open-world is true; the tool does not intentionally submit forms or mutate page elements.
tools.click_browser: Clicks exactly one element selected by a bounded semantic locator. A click can submit forms, purchase, delete, publish, or otherwise irreversibly affect external entities, so destructive and open-world are conservatively true.
tools.fill_browser: Writes bounded caller-supplied text into exactly one semantically located page element. Filling can alter external application state and prepare irreversible actions, so destructive and open-world are conservatively true even though no submit is implicit.
tools.close_browser_session: Closes and destroys one Telechir-managed isolated ephemeral browser session. The local session state is intentionally destroyed, so destructive is true; the action does not itself access an open-ended external entity.
